# Why

Spike-in controls are added at amounts we know. Most pipelines use them
once, to normalise or to check one experiment. spikeWatch uses the same
known amounts to score every run, the same way every time, and to watch
those scores across runs so that a run that drifts is flagged.

The known amounts live in an assay beside the measurements. That one idea
covers both kinds of design:

* feature-level designs, where each spike has its own amount, such as the
  ERCC RNA mixes;
* sample-level designs, where the amount changes from sample to sample,
  such as a UPS1 or peptide dilution series.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("spikeWatch")
```

# A series of runs

`simulateSpikeRuns()` makes count data for runs of one ERCC mix, with
sequencing depth that changes from run to run. Here the dose response
compresses from run 31 on: high spikes read a little lower and low spikes
a little higher.

```{r simulate}
library(spikeWatch)
ercc <- erccDesign()
runs <- simulateSpikeRuns(ercc, nRuns = 40, mix = "Mix1", driftAt = 31,
                          driftType = "slope", driftSize = -0.1,
                          seed = 7)
runs
```

The experiment already has its truth attached. For your own data, build or
load a design and call `addTruth()`; see the next section.

# Per-run accuracy

```{r metrics}
m <- runMetrics(runs, minAmount = 1)
head(m, 3)
```

`slope` near 1 means the measured values follow the known amounts.
`minAmount` keeps spikes near the detection limit out of the fit: they are
seen only when their count happens to be high, which would pull the slope
down and tie it to depth. The detection limit `lod` always uses every
spike.

```{r doseplot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
plotDoseResponse(runs, 1)
```

# Drift across runs

The first 20 runs are the baseline. A CUSUM chart on the slope flags the
drift:

```{r chart, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5}
ch <- driftChart(m, "slope", baseline = 20, method = "cusum")
firstSignal(ch)
plotDrift(ch, "Dose-response slope, CUSUM")
```

`driftChart()` also offers EWMA and Shewhart charts, and can chart any
column of `runMetrics()`: `residSD` for precision, `offset` for overall
response, `lod` for sensitivity at the low end.

# Your own data

Rows of the experiment must be named by spike identifier, and `colData`
must say which mix each sample received:

```{r own}
library(SummarizedExperiment)
counts <- assay(runs, "counts")
se <- SummarizedExperiment(list(counts = counts),
                           colData = DataFrame(mix = rep("Mix1", 40)))
se <- addTruth(se, ercc, mix = "mix")
identical(assay(se, "expected"), assay(runs, "expected"))
```

For a dilution series, give each sample a dose and the design one amount
per spike:

```{r dose}
d <- spikeDesign(c("p1", "p2", "p3"), amount = c(1, 1, 1), unit = "fmol")
x <- matrix(c(10, 12, 9, 100, 118, 95), nrow = 3,
            dimnames = list(c("p1", "p2", "p3"), c("low", "high")))
s <- SummarizedExperiment(list(area = x),
                          colData = DataFrame(fmol = c(0.5, 5)))
s <- addTruth(s, d, dose = "fmol")
runMetrics(s)[, c("run", "nDetected", "offset")]
```

# Fold-change accuracy

With samples from two mixes, `ratioAccuracy()` compares measured and
expected log2 ratios, spike by spike and per expected ratio:

```{r ratio}
a <- simulateSpikeRuns(ercc, nRuns = 3, mix = "Mix1", seed = 1)
b <- simulateSpikeRuns(ercc, nRuns = 3, mix = "Mix2", seed = 2)
colnames(b) <- paste0("b", 1:3)
ratioAccuracy(cbind(a, b), 1:3, 4:6)$summary
```
